html:
The Muruwari are an Aboriginal people of northern New South Wales and southwest Queensland, in country along the Culgoa and Birrie rivers north of Brewarrina and Bourke.

Their neighbours on the map include the Wayilwan and Wongaibon to the south, the Gamilaraay to the east and the Gunu to the west. Nearby on the Barwon River are the Brewarrina fish traps, ancient stone traps shared by many peoples of the region. Pastoralists moved into the area in the 1840s. The Muruwari language was well recorded in the 1900s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Muruwari are an Aboriginal people of northern New South Wales and southwest Queensland, in country along the Culgoa and Birrie rivers north of Brewarrina and Bourke.
